items.exampleEn: He suffered the indignity of being ignored at his own party.
items.exampleZh: 他在自己的派對上被冷落，覺得很沒面子。

items.exampleEn: The new paperwork rules are burdensome for small shops.
items.exampleZh: 新的文書規定對小商店來說很繁重。

items.exampleEn: My son is so picky that he won't eat anything green.
items.exampleZh: 我兒子很挑食，綠色的東西一概不吃。

items.exampleEn: Her eloquence helped her team win the debate.
items.exampleZh: 她的好口才幫助她的隊伍贏得辯論。

items.exampleEn: To my bewilderment, the shop was closed on a weekday afternoon.
items.exampleZh: 令我困惑的是，那家店在平日下午竟然沒開。

items.exampleEn: The volunteers' selfless work helped hundreds of families.
items.exampleZh: 志工們無私的付出幫助了好幾百個家庭。

items.exampleEn: Politeness costs nothing, but it means a lot.
items.exampleZh: 禮貌不花一毛錢，卻意義重大。

items.exampleEn: My grandfather was thrilled with his birthday gift.
items.exampleZh: 我爺爺對他的生日禮物非常開心。
items.glossZh: 非常興奮的；極為高興的

items.sentenceEn: The fans were thrilled when the band came back on stage.
items.sentenceZh: 樂團回到台上時，歌迷們興奮極了。

items.audioEn: My cat only eats fish from one shop near our house; she's very picky.
items.audioZh: 我的貓只吃我們家附近某一家店的魚，她非常挑嘴。

items.sentenceEn: Out of politeness, he ate the soup even though he didn't like it.
items.sentenceZh: 出於禮貌，雖然他不喜歡那碗湯，還是把它喝了。

items.sentenceEn: The tourists looked at the strange menu in complete bewilderment.
items.sentenceZh: 遊客們一臉困惑地看著那份奇怪的菜單。

items.stemEn: Our grandmother was a ____ woman who always put others first.
items.stemZh: 我們的祖母是一位無私的女性，總是把別人擺在第一位。

items.stemEn: The speaker's ____ moved the whole audience to tears.
items.stemZh: 那位講者的好口才讓全場觀眾感動落淚。

items.passageEn: Mr. Wu, who lives on our street, has run a free reading class for children for ten years. He is known for his generosity, and although the work is often burdensome, he never complains. Some children are picky about books at first, but he finds the right story for each one. He also teaches them politeness, such as thanking the bus driver. Last week, the city gave him an award, and he accepted it with real eloquence. We were all thrilled for him.
items.passageZh: 住在我們這條街的吳先生，十年來為孩子們開免費的閱讀班。他以慷慨聞名，雖然這份工作常常很繁重，他從不抱怨。有些孩子一開始對書很挑，但他總能替每個孩子找到合適的故事。他也教他們禮貌，例如向公車司機道謝。上週，市政府頒獎給他，他發表了一段很動人的感言。我們都替他感到非常高興。

questions.questionZh: 吳先生怎麼對待挑書的孩子？
options: 替每個孩子找合適的故事

questions.questionZh: 吳先生教孩子哪一種禮貌？

items.promptZh: 被當成小偷是一種侮辱。
referenceEn: Being treated like a thief was an indignity.
It was an indignity to be treated as a thief.
rubricZh: 要用 indignity（例如 was an indignity）
「被當成」可寫，例如 being treated like、be treated as 等
時態合理即可（例如 was、is）

items.promptZh: 他們的幫忙完全是無私的，從來不要求任何回報。
referenceEn: Their help was completely selfless; they never asked for anything in return.
Their help was totally selfless, and they never asked for anything back.
rubricZh: selfless 當形容詞（例如 was completely selfless 等）
「不要求任何回報」可寫，例如 never asked for anything in return 等
時態可用過去式或現在式（例如 was、is、asked、ask 等）
